Read-only research task against Confluence (zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net, space SFCC — key "SFCC"). Do NOT modify/create/comment on anything. If mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_* tools are deferred, load them first via ToolSearch: "select:mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_search,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_page,mcp__mcp-atlassian__confluence_get_comments".

CONTEXT: There is an open design disagreement documented as inline comments on Confluence page 346783750 ("Contentful Integration Technical Design & Content Model (SFCC-249)"), section 5.5. The TSD proposes a rule splitting Contentful-consuming components into two authoring paths: "Studio Experience" components (used inside Contentful's drag-and-drop "Experience Builder" tool, for whole author-composed pages like Z.immerse/campaign landing pages) versus "coded content-type components" (hand-built React components for fixed slots in commerce templates like homepage/footer/nav/PLP/PDP). Tim Lavelle (Solution Architect) commented pushing back: "I'm not sure we need to separate these and the components we build will most of the time being used in an experience builder" and "Authors will place elements on a page" — suggesting he may want MOST or ALL components built for the Experience Builder rather than maintaining two separate paths.

TASK: Search Confluence space SFCC exhaustively for ANY clue about the intended direction here — i.e., any page, requirement, or decision that reveals whether Zimmermann/Accenture plans to use the Experience Builder broadly (for footer, nav, homepage, PLP, PDP, etc., not just Z.immerse/campaign pages) versus keeping most components as hand-coded.

Specifically check/search:
1. confluence_search for terms: "Experience Builder", "Studio Experience", "experience builder", "component library", "flexible components", "page composition", "visual editor", "drag and drop", "authoring experience".
2. Re-read SFCC-10-adjacent or Z.immerse-adjacent Confluence pages if any exist (search "Z.immerse", "immerse").
3. Re-read page 318472193 ("Contentful CMS — Setup & Operations") IN FULL if not already — does it say anything about which content types use the Experience Builder vs coded components, or a stated strategy/roadmap?
4. Search for any "Enterprise Onboarding" or Contentful vendor-provided strategy documents in the space (there was an attachment "Zimmermann - Enterprise Onboarding Kickoff.pdf" seen before — check if that or similar docs discuss Experience Builder as the primary authoring paradigm Contentful/Zimmermann agreed to).
5. Search Confluence comments (not just page bodies) across any Contentful-related pages for Tim Lavelle's prior statements about component architecture, authoring strategy, or "most content built via X".
6. Check page 303071234 ("04.1.1 Homepage and Content") and any related 04.1.x pages for requirements language about how homepage/footer/nav modules should be authored (does it specify Experience Builder vs fixed templates?).
7. Any discovery-phase or kickoff documents (e.g. "Zimmermann Digital Modernisation" / "Final Deliverables" deck) that describe the intended CMS authoring model at a strategic level.

Report back ONLY concrete findings with page-id + exact quote. If searches turn up nothing relevant to this FUTURE-DIRECTION question, say so explicitly per search rather than padding with tangential results. Do not speculate about what Tim "probably" means.
